The compensation must not exceed the current value of the improvements.

If the Minister administering the Crown Land Management Act 2016 and the local authority or Local Land Services are unable to reach an agreement as to the amount of compensation payable under this section, either of them may apply to the Civil and Administrative Tribunal to determine the matter.
The Tribunal to which application is made under this section must determine the amount of compensation payable.
The controlling authority of a stock watering place may, following auction, public tender or other means approved by Local Land Services, grant a lease of the watering place.

The controlling authority must not grant a lease of a stock watering place for a period (including any period for which the lease could be extended or renewed by the exercise of an option) exceeding the period prescribed by the regulations.
A lease of a stock watering place may, with the approval of the controlling authority of that place, be transferred to another person.

heading.b: Controlling authority and lessee to supply water to certain persons and stock

block.txt: The controlling authority, or lessee, of a stock watering place must—
supply water (if available) to any person or stock of a class prescribed by the regulations, or
allow stock to depasture at the stock watering place in the circumstances, and in accordance with any conditions, prescribed by the regulations.

heading.b: Offence to damage stock watering place

block.txt: A person must not intentionally or recklessly pollute or, without lawful authority, interfere with any water that flows into, or that is used as, the source of supply for any stock watering place.
Maximum penalty—100 penalty units.

If any person pollutes or, without lawful authority, interferes with any water that flows into, or that is used as, the source of supply for a stock watering place, the relevant controlling authority may recover from the person an amount equal to the cost of cleaning up or removing the pollution or interference as a debt due in a court of competent jurisdiction.
Proceedings may be brought under subsection (2) irrespective of whether proceedings could be or have been brought for an offence under subsection (1) arising out of the same matter.

heading.b: Impounding of unattended and trespassing stock and abandoned items

block.txt: The Public Spaces (Unattended Property) Act 2021 empowers persons appointed by Local Land Services (which is an authority for the purposes of that Act) to impound and deal with animals (including pigs and deer) and items in public places and places owned or under the control of Local Land Services if, in the case of animals, they are unattended or trespassing or, in the case of items, they have been abandoned or left unattended. It also enables occupiers of private land to impound and deal with animals trespassing on their land, provides for the release of impounded animals and items that are claimed by their owners and, if they are disposed of by sale, provides for the disposal of the proceeds of sale.
This Part includes some provisions that complement or supplement the provisions of the Public Spaces (Unattended Property) Act 2021.
In this Part—
impound means to take possession of an animal under—
this part or,
the Public Spaces (Unattended Property) Act 2021.
stock includes pig and deer.

If an expression is defined in the Public Spaces (Unattended Property) Act 2021 and is also used in this Part, the expression as used in this Part has, unless the contrary intention appears, the same meaning as in that Act.
Expressions used include—
authority, which is defined to include Local Land Services.
unattended which is defined, in relation to an animal, to include abandoned or straying.
Stock are not unattended for the Public Spaces (Unattended Property) Act 2021, sections 18(2)(d) and 37(4)(d) if the stock are unattended on a road or travelling stock reserve—
in accordance with the authority conferred by (and any conditions of) a stock permit, or
in any other circumstances prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this paragraph.

heading.b: Offence of causing or permitting stock to be on a public road, travelling stock reserve or public land without authority

block.txt: If stock (whether attended or unattended) are on a public road, travelling stock reserve or other public land except in accordance with the authority conferred by (and in accordance with any conditions of) a stock permit or by or under any law the owner of the stock, and the person in charge of the stock (if not the owner), are each guilty of an offence.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.
It is a defence to a prosecution for an offence against this section if the defendant proves that the defendant had taken all reasonable steps to prevent the contravention.

An authorised officer may impound any stock the authorised officer suspects to be on a public road, travelling stock reserve or other public land in contravention of this section in the same way that the authorised officer may impound an animal under the Public Spaces (Unattended Property) Act 2021, section 18.
A person must not, without the authority of an authority—
release, or
incite or assist any person to release,
any animal impounded, or seized or detained in a region for the purpose of this part or the Public Spaces (Unattended Property) Act 2021.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.
In this Part—
Accreditation Committee means the Stock Transportation Accreditation Committee constituted by section 125.
authorised officer means an authorised officer who is—
a police officer, or
an authorised officer who is authorised to exercise functions conferred on authorised officers by this Part.
stock means the following—
cattle,
sheep,
any other kind of animal declared by the regulations to be stock for the purposes of this Part.
stock transportation particulars—see section 119.
Vehicle is defined in the Dictionary to this Act to include any means of road, rail, waterborne or airborne transport.
transported stock statement means a document that contains stock transportation particulars and that is in a form approved for the purposes of this Part under section 127.
For the purposes of this Part, the following are stock transportation particulars in relation to stock—
the date the transportation of the stock commenced or is to commence,
the address at which the stock were or are to be loaded to commence the transportation,
details of the type and number of stock being or to be transported,

if the stock are being or are to be transported for the owner or owners of the stock—the name and address of the owner of the stock (or, if there is more than one owner, of at least one of the owners),

if the stock are being or are to be transported for a person other than the owner or owners of the stock who is an employee of the owner or owners or is otherwise responsible for the stock—the name and address of that person,
the name and address of the person to whom the stock are being or are to be transported,
the address to which the stock are being or are to be transported (if different from the address referred to in paragraph (f)),
any other particulars prescribed by the regulations.
In this section—
address of a corporation means the registered office or sole or principal place of business of the corporation.

heading.b: Restrictions on the transport of stock by vehicle on road

block.txt: An owner of stock that are to be transported by a vehicle on a road must—
duly complete a transported stock statement in relation to the stock, and
if a person other than an owner is to transport the stock, make a copy of the statement,
before the commencement of the transportation.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
Section 122 requires records of transported stock statements to be retained.

If the owner of stock causes another person to transport the stock by vehicle on a road, the owner must provide the person in charge of the vehicle at the commencement of the transportation with a transported stock statement in relation to the stock before the commencement of the transportation.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
The person who is in charge of a vehicle in which stock are being transported on a road must—
be in possession of a transported stock statement in relation to the stock, and
ensure that the stock correspond with the description of the stock specified in the document.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
A person is not guilty of an offence under this section if the stock concerned are transported or are to be transported under the authority of—
a stock permit, or
an order, biosecurity direction, permit or biosecurity zone regulation under the Biosecurity Act 2015.
This section does not apply to the transport of stock by vehicle on a road in the following circumstances—

stock transported into New South Wales from another State or the Australian Capital Territory and transported within New South Wales for up to 30 kilometres before proceeding back into the other State or that Territory as part of an unbroken journey,
stock transported across or along a road from one part of a holding to another part that would be contiguous with the first-mentioned part but for being separated by the road,
stock transported to or from a place for treatment by a veterinary practitioner (within the meaning of the Veterinary Practice Act 2003),
stock transported in any other circumstances prescribed by the regulations.
In this section—
owner of stock includes—
an employee of the owner of the stock, and
a person other than the owner of the stock who is responsible for the stock, and
an employee of a person referred to in paragraph (b).

heading.b: Restriction on the consignment of stock by rail, water or air transport

block.txt: A person must not consign stock that are to be transported by any form of rail, water or air transport to another person (the consignee) unless the person has provided the consignee with a duly completed transported stock statement in respect of the stock.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

A consignee who is provided with a transported stock statement must (unless the consignee is to be responsible for the stock during the transport) provide a copy of the statement to the person who is to be responsible for the stock during the transport.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
A person who is provided by a consignee with a copy of a transported stock statement under subsection (2) must be in possession of the copy until the end of the transport of the stock concerned.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
A person is not guilty of an offence under this section if the stock concerned are consigned under the authority of—
a stock permit, or
an order, biosecurity direction, permit or biosecurity zone regulation under the Biosecurity Act 2015.

heading.b: Records of transported stock statements to be retained

block.txt: An owner of stock who completes a transported stock statement under section 120 (1) in relation to stock that the owner transports by a vehicle must retain the statement for at least 2 years after the day on which the transportation ends.

An owner of stock who provides another person with a transported stock statement under section 120 (2) or 121 (1) must retain a copy of the statement for at least 2 years after the day on which the transportation ends.
A person in charge of a vehicle who is provided with a transported stock statement under section 120 (2) must retain the statement for at least 2 years after the day the transportation ends.
A consignee who is provided with a transported stock statement under section 121 must retain the statement for at least 2 years after the day on which it is provided.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

heading.b: Powers to stop and search vehicles transporting stock

block.txt: An authorised officer may exercise any one or more of the vehicle search powers in respect of a vehicle if the authorised officer has reasonable grounds to believe that the vehicle is being used to transport stock.
An authorised officer who exercises a vehicle search power under this section has the power to give reasonable directions (to facilitate the exercise of the power) to any person—
in or on the vehicle concerned, or
in the vicinity of the vehicle concerned.

heading.b: Preconditions for exercise of vehicle search power

block.txt: An authorised officer may give a direction referred to in subsection (2) only if, before giving the direction, the authorised officer—
provides evidence to the person that he or she is an authorised officer (unless the authorised officer is a police officer in uniform), and
in the case of a police officer in uniform—provides his or her name and place of duty, and
informs the person of the reason for the direction, and
warns the person that a failure to comply with the direction may be an offence.
A person must (unless the person has a reasonable excuse for not doing so)—
stop a vehicle the person is in charge of when directed under this section to do so by an authorised officer, or
comply with any other direction given under this section by an authorised officer.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units or 12 months imprisonment, or both.
In this section—
vehicle search power means any of the following powers—
a power to stop a vehicle transporting stock for the purposes of determining whether or not—
the person in charge of the vehicle is in possession of the transported stock statements required by section 120, or
the person responsible for the stock is in possession of the transported stock statements required by section 121 (2),
the power to inspect any of the statements referred to in paragraph (a),

the power to search a vehicle (whether or not stopped under paragraph (a)) transporting stock for the purposes of determining whether stock being transported appear to be the stock to which transported stock statements in the possession of the person in charge of the vehicle, or who is responsible for the stock, relate and to give reasonable directions to any person in the vehicle for the purpose of facilitating the search,

the power to take possession of any stock or object found in the course of such a search that the authorised officer conducting the search suspects on reasonable grounds constitutes evidence of an offence under this Act or under any other law.

heading.b: Person in charge of vehicle transporting stock to give name and other particulars

block.txt: An authorised officer may request the person in charge of a vehicle that the authorised officer has reasonable grounds to believe is being used to transport stock to give the person’s name or residential address, or both.
An authorised officer may make a request referred to in subsection (1) only if, before making the request, the authorised officer—
provides evidence to the person that he or she is an authorised officer (unless the authorised officer is a police officer in uniform), and
in the case of a police officer in uniform—provides his or her name and place of duty, and
informs the person of the reason for the request, and
warns the person that a failure to comply with the request may be an offence.
A person who (without reasonable excuse)—
fails to comply with a request under this section, or
in response to the request, gives a name or address that is false or misleading,
is guilty of an offence.
Maximum penalty—10 penalty units.
There is constituted by this section a Stock Transportation Accreditation Committee.
The Accreditation Committee consists of 3 members of whom—
one is to be a person nominated by the Secretary, and
one is to be a person nominated by the Commissioner of Police, and
one is to be a person nominated by the Livestock and Bulk Carriers Association Incorporated.
The member referred to in subsection (2) (b) is to be the Chairperson of the Accreditation Committee.
The Accreditation Committee has such functions as are conferred or imposed on the Committee by or under this Act.

The procedure for the calling of meetings of the Accreditation Committee, and for the conduct of business at those meetings is, subject to this Act and the regulations, to be as determined by the Committee.
Two members constitute a quorum at a meeting of the Committee.
A decision supported by a majority of the votes cast at a meeting of the Committee at which a quorum is present is the decision of the Committee.
The Chairperson has a deliberative vote and, in the event of an equality of votes, has a second or casting vote.
An application for approval of the form of a consignment note or other document as a transported stock statement made to the Accreditation Committee must be—
made in such manner and form as the Accreditation Committee may approve, and
supported by such information as the Accreditation Committee may require, and
accompanied by the application fee (if any) prescribed by the regulations.

The Accreditation Committee may require an applicant to furnish to the Accreditation Committee, within such time as may be specified, such further particulars as the Accreditation Committee considers necessary to determine the suitability of the proposed form of consignment note or other document for accreditation.

heading.b: Approval of form of transported stock statement

block.txt: The Accreditation Committee may, by order in writing, approve as a transported stock statement a form of consignment note or other document for the purposes of this Part on application made to the Committee under section 126.
The Secretary may, by order published in the Gazette, approve as a transported stock statement a consignment note or other document for the purposes of this Part.
An approval may be given subject to the condition that a document be compiled or identified in a manner specified by the Accreditation Committee or Secretary.

An authorised officer may enter any premises to enable the authorised officer to exercise any function conferred or imposed on the authorised officer, or any function of Local Land Services that the officer is authorised to exercise, by or under this Act.

The authorised officer may enter premises with such persons and with such vehicles, horses and dogs as the authorised officer considers are necessary to enable or assist the authorised officer to exercise the function concerned.

heading.b: Purposes for which powers under Part may be exercised

block.txt: Powers may be exercised under this Part for the following purposes—
for determining whether there has been compliance with or a contravention of this Act or the regulations or any order, licence, notice, permit or requirement issued or made under this Act,
for obtaining information or records for purposes connected with the administration of this Act,
for the purpose of enabling Local Land Services, the authorised officer or any other person to exercise any function conferred or imposed on the person under this or any other Act.
Nothing in this Part affects any function under any other Part of this Act.
An authorising authority may appoint a police officer or any other person (including a class of persons) as an authorised officer for the purposes of this Act.
Authorising authority is defined in the Dictionary.
An authorisation of a person as an authorised officer can be given generally, or subject to conditions, limitations or restrictions or only for limited purposes.

The authority of an authorised officer may be limited by the relevant instrument of appointment to the functions, or the exercise of functions in such region or part of a region, as are specified in the instrument of appointment.

If such authorisation is given subject to conditions, limitations or restrictions or only for limited purposes, nothing in this Act authorises or requires the authorised officer to act in contravention of the conditions, limitations or restrictions or for other purposes.
Every authorised officer, other than a police officer, is to be provided by the authorising authority with an identification card.

In the course of exercising the functions of an authorised officer under this Act, an authorised officer, other than a police officer, must, if requested to do so by any person affected by the exercise of the functions, produce the officer’s identification card to the person.

In the course of exercising the functions of an authorised officer under this Act, an authorised officer who is a police officer must, if requested to do so by any person affected by the exercise of the functions, produce his or her identification as a police officer (unless he or she is in uniform).
An identification card is a card or document that—
states that it is issued under this Act, and
gives the name of the person to whom it is issued, and
describes the nature of the powers conferred and the source of the powers, and
states the date (if any) on which it expires, and
describes the kind of premises to which the power extends, and
bears the signature of the person prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this paragraph.
An authorised officer may enter any premises at any reasonable time.

heading.b: Entry into residential premises only with permission or warrant

block.txt: This Part does not empower an authorised officer to enter any part of premises used only for residential purposes without the permission of the occupier or the authority of a search warrant issued under section 178.

heading.b: Powers of authorised officers to do things on premises

block.txt: An authorised officer may, at any premises lawfully entered, do anything that in the opinion of the authorised officer is necessary to be done for the purposes of this Act, including (but not limited to) the things specified in subsection (2).
An authorised officer who enters premises may do any or all of the following—
inspect the premises,
search the premises,
examine, seize, detain or remove any pest in or about those premises,
examine, seize, detain or remove any other thing that the authorised officer has reasonable grounds to believe is being used to contravene this Act or the regulations,
require the production of and inspect any records in or about those premises,
take copies of, or extracts or notes from, any such records,
require any person in or about those premises to answer questions or otherwise furnish information,

require the occupier of those premises to provide the authorised officer with such assistance and facilities as are reasonably necessary to enable the authorised officer to exercise his or her functions,
remove or destroy or cause to be removed or destroyed any pest found in or about those premises that is being kept in captivity without lawful authority,
break open and search any box, container, package or receptacle (including any place that could be used as a receptacle) in or about those premises,
examine or muster any stock.

Before an authorised officer enters premises under this Part, the authorising authority must give the occupier of the premises oral or written notice of the intention to enter the occupier’s premises on a day or within a period of days specified in the notice.
The day or any day within the period of days specified must not be the day on which the notice is given.
This section does not require notice to be given—
if entry to the premises is made with the consent of the occupier of the premises, or
if entry has been authorised by a search warrant issued under section 178, or
if entry is required urgently and the authorising authority has authorised in writing (either generally or in the particular case) entry without notice, or
if the authorised officer concerned is a police officer and the giving of notice would defeat the purpose for which it is intended to exercise the power of entry, or
if entry is required to eradicate any pest kept in captivity without lawful authority.

Reasonable force may be used for the purpose of gaining entry to any premises (other than residential premises) under a power conferred by this Part but only if authorised by the authorising authority in accordance with this section and in accordance with any guidelines.

No force is to be exercised in any case unless the authorising authority has authorised in writing (either in a specified class of cases or in the particular case) the use of force in the circumstances of the case.
A general authority given by the authorising authority for the use of force is invalid. The authority is to specify the circumstances that are required to exist in a case before force is used.

heading.b: Notification of use of force or urgent entry

block.txt: An authorised officer must give the authorising authority prompt oral or written advice of—
any use of force by the authorised officer for the purpose of gaining entry to premises, or
any entry to premises by the authorised officer without notice having been given to the occupier of the premises of the intention to enter as required by section 173.
The authorising authority must give notice of the entry to such persons or authorities as appear to be appropriate in the circumstances.
In the exercise of a function under this Part, an authorised officer must do as little damage as possible.

An authorising authority must compensate all interested parties for any damage caused by an authorised officer who enters premises under this Part in entering the premises (but not any damage caused by exercising any other function), unless the occupier of the premises obstructed, hindered or restricted the authorised officer in the exercise of the power of entry.

An authorised officer under this Act may apply to an authorised officer within the meaning of the Law Enforcement (Powers and Responsibilities) Act 2002 for a search warrant if the authorised officer under this Act has reasonable grounds for believing that a provision of this Act or the regulations has been or is being or is about to be contravened in or about any premises.

An authorised officer under this Act may not apply for a search warrant to search premises unless the authorised officer under this Act has notified the authorising authority of the intended application.

An authorised officer within the meaning of the Law Enforcement (Powers and Responsibilities) Act 2002 to whom an application is made under this section may, if satisfied that there are reasonable grounds for doing so, issue a warrant authorising an authorised officer under this Act named in the warrant to enter the premises and to exercise there the powers under section 172.
Division 4 of Part 5 of the Law Enforcement (Powers and Responsibilities) Act 2002 applies to a search warrant issued under this section.

An authorised officer may request the assistance of any police officer if the authorised officer reasonably believes that the performance of functions conferred or imposed by or under this Act will be obstructed.

An authorised officer may request the assistance of any person the authorised officer believes to be capable of providing assistance in the performance of functions conferred or imposed by or under this Act.

heading.b: Offences in relation to authorised officers

block.txt: A person who—
prevents an authorised officer from exercising a function conferred or imposed by or under this Act, or
hinders, obstructs, threatens or assaults an authorised officer in the exercise of such a function, or
without reasonable excuse, refuses or fails to comply with a requirement made or to answer a question of an authorised officer asked in accordance with this Act or the regulations, or
furnishes an authorised officer with information knowing that it is false or misleading in a material particular,
is guilty of an offence.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.
A person is not guilty of an offence under subsection (1) (c) unless it is established that, at the material time, the authorised officer—
identified himself or herself as an authorised officer, and
warned the person that a failure or refusal to comply with the requirement may constitute an offence.

heading.b: Offence: impersonating authorised officer or other authorised person

block.txt: A person who impersonates or falsely represents that the person is an authorised officer is guilty of an offence.
Maximum penalty—10 penalty units.

heading.b: Recovery of outstanding rates, charges and other amounts
Sale of land for unpaid amounts owing to Local Land Services

block.txt: Local Land Services may sell land to recover unpaid rates, levies or contributions of a kind prescribed by the regulations owing to it in accordance with Schedule 5.

heading.b: Recovery of rates, charges, fees and other unpaid amounts

block.txt: Any rate, charge, fee or other money due or payable to Local Land Services or any other person under this Act may be recovered by Local Land Services or the person as a debt in a court of competent jurisdiction.

The amount of any judgment that is recovered in proceedings brought under this section, and of any costs awarded to Local Land Services or other person concerned in respect of the proceedings, is a charge on any land (other than public land) concerned.

Schedule 5 applies to an amount or any part of an amount awarded or ordered to be paid to Local Land Services or any other person under this section that remains unpaid after the expiration of 5 years from the date of the judgment or order of the court concerned.
The provisions of this section have effect despite anything contained in section 42 of the Real Property Act 1900.

heading.b: Accrual of interest on overdue rates, charges and other amounts

block.txt: Interest accrues on rates, charges and other amounts payable to an authority, the Minister or any other person under this Act.
Interest accrues on a daily basis or on such other basis as is determined by Local Land Services or the person concerned.
The rate of interest is that set by Local Land Services or the person concerned but must not exceed the rate specified for the time being by the Minister by notice published in the Gazette.
Accrued interest is, for the purpose of its recovery, taken to be a rate, charge or amount that is due and payable.

Interest continues to accrue on unpaid rates, charges or amounts even though judgment for payment of the rates, charges or amounts may have been obtained in a court. Interest is not payable on the judgment debt, despite any other Act.

heading.b: Special provision with respect to recovery of unpaid rates and charges

block.txt: Despite anything to the contrary in the Limitation Act 1969, proceedings for the recovery of a rate or charge may be commenced at any time within 20 years after the date when the rate or charge becomes payable.

heading.b: Rebates, waiver, refund or writing off of rates, charges and other amounts

block.txt: Local Land Services may do any one or more of the following—
grant a rebate or waive payment of a rate, charge or other amount due or payable to it under this Act or the regulations or any part of such a rate, charge or other amount,
refund any rate, charge or other amount in whole or in part,
write off any rate, charge or other amount.
Action under this section may be taken in a particular case or class of cases.
Proceedings for an offence against this Act or the regulations are to be dealt with summarily before the Local Court.
Proceedings for an offence against this Act may instead be dealt with summarily before the Supreme Court in its summary jurisdiction.
The maximum monetary penalty that may be imposed by the Local Court in proceedings for an offence against this Act or the regulations is 100 penalty units.
The maximum penalty that may be imposed by the Supreme Court in proceedings for an offence against this Act is the maximum penalty specified by the relevant section in respect of the offence.

heading.b: Time within which summary proceedings may be commenced

block.txt: Proceedings for an offence under this Act or the regulations may be commenced—
in the case of a prescribed offence—within but not later than 2 years after the day on which the offence is alleged to have been committed, or
in any other case—within but not later than 12 months after that day.
This section applies only to proceedings that are to be dealt with summarily.
This section applies despite anything in the Criminal Procedure Act 1986 or any other Act.
In this section—
prescribed offence means—
an offence arising under section 58 (Annual returns of land and stock),
an offence against this Act that is declared by the regulations to be a prescribed offence for the purposes of this section.
An authorised officer may issue a penalty notice to a person if it appears to the officer that the person has committed a penalty notice offence.
A penalty notice offence is an offence against this Act or the regulations that is prescribed by the regulations as a penalty notice offence.
The Fines Act 1996 applies to a penalty notice issued under this section.

The Fines Act 1996 provides that, if a person issued with a penalty notice does not wish to have the matter determined by a court, the person may pay the amount specified in the notice and is not liable to any further proceedings for the alleged offence.

The amount payable under a penalty notice issued under this section is the amount prescribed for the alleged offence by the regulations (not exceeding the maximum amount of penalty that could be imposed for the offence by a court).
This section does not limit the operation of any other provision of, or made under, this or any other Act relating to proceedings that may be taken in respect of offences.

heading.b: Penalties belong to Local Land Services

block.txt: Whenever any monetary penalty is imposed for an offence against this Act that is prosecuted by Local Land Services the proper officer of the court that imposed the penalty must pay the amount of the penalty to Local Land Services.

An amount paid to Local Land Services under this section, or paid under section 189 for a penalty payable under a penalty notice served by an authorised officer appointed by Local Land Services, belongs to Local Land Services.
This section applies irrespective of any other law to the contrary.

heading.b: Court may order payment of additional penalty in certain cases

block.txt: A court that finds a person guilty of an offence under a prescribed section (whether or not it convicts the person of the offence), may, in addition to any other penalty that it may impose, order the person to pay to Local Land Services an amount sufficient to reimburse or compensate Local Land Services for any expenses (including any costs of agistment) incurred or losses suffered by Local Land Services as a result of the offence.
In this section—
prescribed section means any of the following sections—
section 84 (Movement and grazing of stock authorised by stock permits must comply with Act and regulations), or
section 116 (Offence of causing or permitting stock to be on a public road, travelling stock reserve or public land without authority).

heading.b: Offences relating to provision of information in relation to certain matters

block.txt: A person who, having been required under a provision of this Act or the regulations to provide information, fails without reasonable excuse to provide that information is guilty of an offence.
Maximum penalty—10 penalty units.

A person must not make a statement for the purposes of this Act to a person engaged in the administration of this Act, or make a statement in an official document under this Act, that the person knows—
is false or misleading in a material respect, or
omits material matter.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

A document is an official document under this Act if it is an application, return, declaration or other document that is required to be given to the Minister, the Board, Local Land Services, the Secretary or an authorised officer for the purposes of this Act or the regulations.
A person who forges or fraudulently alters any permit, licence, authority or other document issued or purporting to be issued under this Act is guilty of an offence.
Maximum penalty—100 penalty units.

heading.b: Onus of proof concerning reasonable or lawful excuse

block.txt: In any proceedings under this Act, the onus of proving that a person had a reasonable or lawful excuse (as referred to in any provision of this Act or the regulations) lies with the defendant.
See also sections 156 (Public documents) and 158 (Evidence of certain public documents) of the Evidence Act 1995 in relation to proof of various matters in proceedings under this Act.

heading.b: General description of land sufficient for purposes of legal proceedings

block.txt: For the purposes of any proceedings, or an order, notice or permit given, under this Act or the regulations—
a holding or land need not be described by metes and bounds, and
it is sufficient if the holding or land is referred to by its name, location or boundaries or in any other way that adequately identifies it.

heading.b: Legal proceedings against an occupier or owner whose name is unknown

block.txt: If the name of the occupier or owner of a holding or land is unknown to a person who wishes to serve a notice or other document or bring proceedings against that occupier or owner under this Act, the notice or document may be served on, or the proceedings may be brought against, the occupier or owner of the holding or land without specifying the name of that occupier or owner.

heading.b: Jurisdiction of court or NCAT not to be ousted in certain proceedings

block.txt: The jurisdiction of a court or the Civil and Administrative Tribunal is not affected merely because, in proceedings before the court or board under or for the purposes of this Act or the regulations, a question arises concerning—
title to land, or
any matter in which rights in future may be bound, or
any general right or duty.
A decision of a court or the Civil and Administrative Tribunal relating to such a question is not evidence in any other court or in any other legal proceeding.

heading.b: Proof of certain matters not required

block.txt: In any proceedings under this Act, proof is not required (unless evidence is given to the contrary) of any of the following—
the constitution of the Board or a local board,
any resolution of the Board or a local board,
the election or appointment of, or holding of office by, a member of the Board or a local board,
the presence of a quorum at a meeting of the Board or a local board,
the constitution of a particular region,
the boundaries of a region or of a part of a region,
the fact that specified land or a specified place is or is not within a particular region or a particular part of a region,
the appointment of any district veterinarian or any other member of staff of Local Land Services,

the fact that the defendant is, or at any relevant time was, the occupier, owner, manager or caretaker of a holding or land to which the proceedings relate if the defendant is so described in the process by which the proceedings were initiated,
the fact that a holding or land to which the proceedings relate is within the jurisdiction of a particular court or the Civil and Administrative Tribunal,
the notification, dedication, reservation or declaration of a travelling stock reserve or stock watering place.

heading.b: Administration of functions of Local Land Services or local board
Appointment of administrator of all or some functions of Local Land Services

block.txt: The Minister may, by order published in the Gazette, appoint a person specified in the order as administrator of—
all of the functions of Local Land Services, or
one or more (but not all) of the functions of Local Land Services specified in the order.
An order may be made—
if the Board has failed to comply with any direction of the Minister, or to carry out to the satisfaction of the Minister, any of its functions, or
in such other circumstances as may be prescribed by the regulations.

heading.b: Appointment of administrator of all or some functions of local boards

block.txt: The Minister may, by order published in the Gazette, appoint a person specified in the order as administrator of—
all of the functions of a local board, or
one or more (but not all) of the functions of a local board specified in the order.
An order may be made—
if the local board has failed to comply with any direction of Local Land Services or to carry out any of its functions to the satisfaction of Local Land Services, or
in such other circumstances as may be prescribed by the regulations.
The administrator holds office (subject to this Act) for such period as may be specified in the administrator’s instrument of appointment.

An administrator appointed under this Part has and may exercise, subject to any conditions specified in the order appointing the administrator, the functions of Local Land Services or the local board specified in the order.

Any delegation or authority made or conferred by the Board in respect of any function of Local Land Services that may be exercised by an administrator appointed under this Part ceases to have effect on that appointment.

Any delegation or authority made or conferred by a local board in respect of any function of the local board that may be exercised by an administrator appointed under this Part ceases to have effect on that appointment.
The regulations may make provision for or with respect to administrators appointed under this Part.
Schedule 4 has effect with respect to an administrator appointed under this Part.

heading.b: Contributions towards management of pests under Biosecurity Act 2015

block.txt: The Biosecurity Minister may, by notice, require Local Land Services to pay to the Biosecurity Minister an amount as a contribution to the cost of any action taken or to be taken to manage pests under the Biosecurity Act 2015.
A contribution is payable within such period after the notice is given as is specified in the notice or within such other period as the Biosecurity Minister allows.
Any contribution that remains unpaid is recoverable by the Biosecurity Minister from Local Land Services in a court of competent jurisdiction.
The regulations may make provision for or with respect to notices and contributions under this section.
The Biosecurity Minister may delegate to a person employed in the Department any of the Biosecurity Minister’s functions under this section, other than this power of delegation.
In this section—
Biosecurity Minister means the Minister administering the Biosecurity Act 2015.
manage a pest means to prevent, eliminate, minimise or manage the biosecurity risk posed by, or the biosecurity impact of, a pest, within the meaning of the Biosecurity Act 2015.
pest means a pest within the meaning of the Biosecurity Act 2015 (other than a pest that is a plant).
Local Land Services may, for the purposes of this Act, acquire land by agreement or compulsory process in accordance with the Land Acquisition (Just Terms Compensation) Act 1991.

For the purposes of the Public Works Act 1912, any such acquisition of land is taken to be for an authorised work and Local Land Services is, in relation to that authorised work, taken to be the Constructing Authority.
Sections 34–37 of the Public Works Act 1912 do not apply in relation to works constructed under this Act.

heading.b: Entry on land for construction of works and other purposes

block.txt: In this section—
construct includes repair or maintain.
work includes any building or structure.

Local Land Services may, by its staff and other persons, enter and inspect any land (other than a dwelling) for the purpose of exercising the following functions, and there construct any work that it is required or authorised by or under this Act to construct on the land—
functions relating to natural resource management,
any other functions prescribed by the regulations.
A person must not, without reasonable excuse, obstruct or hinder Local Land Services acting under this section.
Maximum penalty—10 penalty units.
In relation to land entered or works constructed, Local Land Services—
is to do as little damage as possible in exercising its functions under this section, and
is to compensate all persons who suffer damage by the exercise of those functions.
Compensation may be made by reinstatement or repair, by construction of works or by payment.
A claim for compensation—
is ineffective unless made in writing not later than one year after the damage was suffered, and
in the absence of agreement on the compensation, is to be dealt with as if it were a claim for compensation for the compulsory acquisition of land under this Act.

This section continues entry and construction powers under the Catchment Management Authorities Act 2003 relating to catchment management authorities under that Act (which are replaced by Local Land Services under this Act).

heading.b: Certificate as to rates, charges and other matters

block.txt: Any person may apply to Local Land Services for a certificate as to any of the following matters—
the amount (if any) due or payable to Local Land Services by way of rates, levies, contributions, charges or other amounts in respect of land,
the person liable to pay any amount referred to in paragraph (a),
any other matter prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this section.
The application must be in the approved form and be accompanied by the fee prescribed by the regulations.
Local Land Services is to issue a certificate to the applicant in the approved form containing the information sought.

The production of the certificate is conclusive proof of the matters certified (including in favour of a purchaser in good faith and for value of the land to which the certificate relates that, at the date of its issue, no amounts were payable to Local Land Services in respect of the land other than such amounts as are specified in the certificate).

For the purposes of this section, rates, levies, contributions, charges or other amounts are taken to be due or payable even though the requisite period after service of any relevant rate or other notice may not have expired.

heading.b: Owner of stock may be ordered to muster stock

block.txt: An authorised officer of the Minister or Local Land Services may, with the approval of the Minister or Local Land Services, order a person who owns stock to muster the stock on the person’s holding (or on a designated part of it) or at some other designated place for a purpose and at a time specified in the order.
A person who fails to comply with such an order at the time specified in it is guilty of an offence.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
If a person fails to comply with such an order at the specified time the authorised officer may have the muster carried out at the person’s expense.
The Minister or Local Land Services may recover the expense of having a muster carried out under this section as a debt in any court of competent jurisdiction.
A matter or thing done or omitted to be done by—
the Minister, or
Local Land Services, or
the Secretary, or
the Board or the Chair or any other member of the Board, or
a member of a local board, or
a member of staff of Local Land Services, or
a person acting under the direction of a person or body referred to in paragraphs (a)–(f),

does not, if the matter or thing was done or omitted to be done in good faith for the purposes of executing this Act, subject the Minister, the Secretary, any member of the Board or a local board, a member of staff or a person so acting personally to any action, liability, claim or demand.

The Governor may make regulations, not inconsistent with this Act, for or with respect to any matter that by this Act is required or permitted to be prescribed or that is necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act.
Without limiting subsection (1), regulations may be made for or with respect to the following—
fees, rates, charges and other amounts payable under this Act or the regulations,
the appointment of members of the Board and local boards,
the election of members of local boards,
the conferral of jurisdiction on a court with respect to such elections,
matters of a savings or transitional nature consequent on any amalgamation of regions,
the process of making, and the form and content of, the State strategic plan, local strategic plans and local annual reports,
the walking and grazing of stock,
the erection of signs when stock are walking or grazing on or near a road and the responsibility of drivers in respect of such signs,
the use of travelling stock reserves and the use of any structures or things constructed or kept on those reserves,
the use or lease of any stock watering place,
permits, licences, authorities and other documents for the purposes of this Act or the regulations,
the insurance to be effected and bonds to be given or obtained in connection with the use of such documents,
the identification of stock,
codes of conduct, including contraventions of a code of conduct,
audits and reports required by or under this Act,

conferring jurisdiction on the Civil and Administrative Tribunal to hear and determine appeals against decisions concerning rates, charges and other amounts payable under this Act or the regulations (including assessments for the purposes of such rates, changes and amounts).

The Minister is not to recommend the making of a regulation containing provisions for the purposes of subsection (2) (p) unless the Minister certifies that the Minister administering the Civil and Administrative Tribunal Act 2013 has agreed to the provisions.
The regulations may create an offence punishable by a penalty not exceeding 100 penalty units.

The regulations may exempt from the operation of all or any of the provisions of Parts 5, 6 and 9 any specified land or class of land, any specified person or class of persons or any specified activities or class of activities in such circumstances, and subject to such conditions, as may be specified in the regulations.
A document may be served on Local Land Services by—
leaving it at, or sending it by post to, an office of Local Land Services, or
sending it by electronic transmission to an address or location specified by Local Land Services for the service of documents of that kind.
A document that is authorised or required by this Act or the regulations to be served on any other person may be served by—
in the case of a natural person—
delivering it to the person personally, or

sending it by post to the address specified by the person for the giving or service of documents or, if no such address is specified, the residential or business address of the person last known to the person giving or serving the document, or
sending it by email to an email address specified by the person for the service of documents of that kind, or
in the case of a body corporate—

leaving it with a person apparently of or above the age of 16 years at, or by sending it by post to, the head office, a registered office or a principal office of the body corporate or to an address specified by the body corporate for the giving or service of documents, or
sending it by email to an email address specified by the body corporate for the service of documents of that kind.
Nothing in this section affects the operation of any provision of a law or of the rules of a court authorising a document to be served on a person in any other manner.

heading.b: Review of Act (other than native vegetation provisions)

block.txt: The Minister is to review this Act to determine whether the policy objectives of the Act remain valid and whether the terms of the Act remain appropriate for securing those objectives.

The review is also to determine whether the governance arrangements for Local Land Services, and the composition of the local boards, remain appropriate given current funding arrangements for local land services.
The review is to be undertaken as soon as possible after the period of 5 years from the date of assent to this Act.
A report on the outcome of the review is to be tabled in each House of Parliament within 12 months after the end of the period of 5 years.
Part 5A and Schedules 5A and 5B are not required to be reviewed under this section.

heading.b: Review of native vegetation provisions of this Act

block.txt: The Minister is to review Part 5A and Schedules 5A and 5B to determine whether the policy objectives of those provisions remain valid and whether the terms of those provisions remain appropriate for securing those objectives.
The review is to be undertaken in conjunction with the review of the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016 that is undertaken under that Act by the Minister administering that Act.
The review is to be undertaken as soon as possible after the period of 5 years from the commencement of Part 5A and Schedules 5A and 5B.
A report on the outcome of the review is to be tabled in each House of Parliament within 12 months after the end of the period of 5 years.
